    39	def list_suspects(repo: str | Path, good: str, bad: str, target: str = ".", graph: bool = False) -> list[Suspect]:
    40	    """Commits in good..bad, oldest first. The last one is the bad ref itself.
    41	
    42	    The path filter gives the first prior: a commit that never touched the agent's folder keeps
    43	    a small one. With `graph`, entire-graph refines it for the commits that did, by asking
    44	    whether what they changed is something the agent runs.
    45	    """
    46	    shas = git(repo, "rev-list", "--reverse", "--ancestry-path", f"{good}..{bad}").split()
    47	    prefix = "" if target in (".", "") else target.rstrip("/") + "/"
    48	    suspects = []
    49	    for sha in shas:
    50	        subject, _, trailer = git(
    51	            repo, "show", "-s", "--format=%s%x00%(trailers:key=Entire-Checkpoint,valueonly,separator=%x20)", sha
    52	        ).strip().partition("\x00")
    53	        files = tuple(git(repo, "diff-tree", "--no-commit-id", "--name-only", "-r", "-m", "--first-parent", sha).split("\n"))
    54	        files = tuple(f for f in files if f)
    55	        touches = any(f.startswith(prefix) for f in files)
    56	        prior, alibi = (PRIOR_TOUCHES_TARGET, "") if touches else (PRIOR_ELSEWHERE, "never touched the agent's folder")
    57	        if graph and touches:
    58	            from .graph import alibi as graph_alibi  # imported here because graph.py uses git() from this module
    59	
    60	            prior, reason = graph_alibi(repo, sha, target)
    61	            alibi = reason if prior < 1.0 else ""
    62	        suspects.append(Suspect(
    63	            sha=sha, subject=subject, files=files, checkpoint=trailer.split()[0] if trailer.strip() else None,
    64	            touches_target=touches, prior=prior, alibi=alibi,
    65	        ))

     2

     7	import json

     9	from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass
    10	from datetime import date
    11	from pathlib import Path
    12	
    13	REVERT, PATCH = "revert", "patch"
    14	
    15	KINDS = {
    16	    "prompt": "a change to the agent's instructions",
    17	    "model-settings": "a change to the model or its settings",
    18	    "dependency": "a dependency change",
    19	    "tool-code": "a change to the code of a tool the agent calls",
    20	    "agent-code": "a change to the agent's own code",
    21	    "other": "a change outside the agent's code",
    22	}

    24	
    25	@dataclass
    26	class Ruling:
    27	    kind: str

    29	    decided_on: str
    30	    first_case: str
    31	    culprit: str
    32	    note: str = ""

    34	
    35	def classify(diff: str, files: list[str]) -> str:
    36	    """What kind of change the culprit made, from its diff. Rough on purpose: it only picks which standing ruling applies."""
    37	    changed = [line[1:] for line in diff.splitlines() if line[:1] in "+-" and not line.startswith(("+++", "---"))]
    38	    text = "\n".join(changed)
    39	    names = " ".join(files).lower()
    40	    if re.search(r"(pyproject\.toml|uv\.lock|requirements[\w.-]*\.txt|package(-lock)?\.json)", names) and not re.search(r"\.py\b", names):
    41	        return "dependency"
    42	    if re.search(r"\b(SYSTEM|PROMPT|INSTRUCTIONS)[A-Z_]*\b|system_prompt|\"role\": \"system\"", text) or "prompt" in names:
    43	        return "prompt"
    44	    # A reworded prompt often changes only the string lines inside it, and the name sits in the context.
    45	    only_strings = bool(changed) and all(line.strip()[:1] in "\"'#" or line.strip()[:2] in ('f"', "f'") for line in changed if line.strip())
    46	    if only_strings and re.search(r"\b(SYSTEM|PROMPT|INSTRUCTIONS)[A-Z_]*\b|system_prompt", diff):
    47	        return "prompt"
    48	    if re.search(r"\b(MODEL|temperature|max_tokens|top_p)\b", text):
    49	        return "model-settings"
    50	    # A tool's own lines are often context around the change, so this one reads the whole diff.
    51	    if re.search(r"kind=\"TOOL\"|\bTOOLS\b|def call_tool\b", diff):
    52	        return "tool-code"
    53	    if re.search(r"\.py\b", names):
    54	        return "agent-code"
    55	    return "other"

    58	def path_for(repo: str | Path, kind: str) -> Path:
    59	    return Path(repo) / "rulings" / f"{kind}.json"
    60	
    61	
    62	def recall(repo: str | Path, kind: str) -> Ruling | None:
    63	    path = path_for(repo, kind)
    64	    return Ruling(**json.loads(path.read_text())) if path.is_file() else None

    67	def question(kind: str, subject: str, request: str | None) -> str:
    68	    asked = f' It was asked for with: "{request.strip().splitlines()[0][:160]}"' if request else ""
    69	    return (
    70	        f"The culprit is {KINDS.get(kind, kind)}: \"{subject}\".{asked}\n"
    71	        f"Revert it, or keep what it was for and patch the bug? This answer becomes the rule for every {kind} case. [revert/patch] "
    72	    )

    75	def decide(repo: str | Path, kind: str, case_id: str, culprit: str, subject: str, request: str | None = None,
    76	           answer: str | None = None, ask=None) -> tuple[Ruling, bool]:
    77	    """Return (ruling, asked). Asks only when there is no ruling for this kind yet."""
    78	    known = recall(repo, kind)
    79	    if known:
    80	        return known, False
    81	    if answer is None:
    82	        answer = (ask or input)(question(kind, subject, request))

    84	    if answer not in (REVERT, PATCH):
    85	        raise ValueError(f"the ruling has to be revert or patch, and was {answer!r}")
    86	    ruling = Ruling(kind=kind, ruling=answer, decided_on=date.today().isoformat(), first_case=case_id, culprit=culprit)
    87	    path = path_for(repo, kind)
    88	    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    89	    path.write_text(json.dumps(asdict(ruling), indent=1) + "\n")

     1	"""Alibis from entire-graph: can this commit's changes reach the agent at all?
     2	
     3	`entire graph commit` lists what a commit changed as entities (a function, a module body, a
     4	document) and `entire graph impact` gives a symbol's callers. A commit that only touched the
     5	README, or a helper script the agent never calls, has an alibi and starts with less suspicion.
     6	It is never cleared outright: the lineup can still land on it if the replays say so.
     7	"""
     8	
     9	import json
    10	import subprocess
    11	from pathlib import Path
    12	
    13	from .suspects import git
    14	
    15	REACHES, UNKNOWN, DATA, UNCALLED, DOCS, ELSEWHERE = 1.0, 1.0, 0.6, 0.15, 0.05, 0.05
    16	DOC_LANGUAGES = {"Markdown", "Git Ignore", "Text", "HTML", "CSS"}
    17	CODE_LANGUAGES = {"Python", "TypeScript", "JavaScript", "Go", "Rust", "Java", "Ruby"}
    18	
    19	
    20	def _graph(repo: str | Path, *args: str, timeout: float = 120.0) -> dict | None:
    21	    """Run an entire-graph command that prints JSON. None if the plugin is missing or the call fails."""
    22	    try:
    23	        done = subprocess.run(["entire", "graph", *args], cwd=repo, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout)
    24	    except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired):
    25	        return None
    26	    if done.returncode != 0:
    27	        return None
    28	    try:
    29	        return json.loads(done.stdout)
    30	    except json.JSONDecodeError:
    31	        return None
    32	
    33	
    34	def changes(repo: str | Path, sha: str) -> list[dict] | None:
    35	    """What a commit changed, one entry per entity: {"path", "language", "kind", "name", "type", "dependents"}."""
    36	    found = _graph(repo, "commit", sha, "--json")
    37	    if found is None:
    38	        return None
    39	    out = []
    40	    for file in found.get("files") or []:
    41	        listed = file.get("changes") or [{"kind": "file", "name": file["path"], "type": file.get("status", "M")}]
    42	        for change in listed:
    43	            out.append({
    44	                "path": file["path"], "language": file.get("language") or "", "kind": change.get("kind", ""),
    45	                "name": change.get("name", ""), "type": change.get("type", ""), "dependents": change.get("dependents_count", 0),
    46	            })
    47	    return out
    48	
    49	
    50	def called_from(repo: str | Path, name: str, path: str, entry: str) -> bool | None:
    51	    """Is this symbol called, directly or through one other function, by code in the entry file? None if unknown."""
    52	    found = _graph(repo, "impact", "--symbol", name, "--file", path, "--repo", ".", "--depth", "2", "--limit", "60", "--format", "json", "--head")
    53	    if found is None or not found.get("focus") or found.get("disambiguation_required"):
    54	        return None
    55	    callers = [entry_["endpoint"].get("file_path", "") for entry_ in (found.get("callers") or {}).get("entries", [])]
    56	    return entry in callers
    57	
    58	
    59	def alibi(repo: str | Path, sha: str, target: str, entry: str = "agent.py") -> tuple[float, str]:
    60	    """(prior weight, reason) for one suspect. A weight of 1 means no alibi."""
    61	    prefix = "" if target in (".", "") else target.rstrip("/") + "/"
    62	    entry_path = prefix + entry
    63	    listed = changes(repo, sha)
    64	    if listed is None:
    65	        return UNKNOWN, "entire-graph could not read this commit"
    66	    # Files the graph does not parse (a lockfile, say) are missing from its list. Git knows them.
    67	    seen = {c["path"] for c in listed}
    68	    for path in git(repo, "diff-tree", "--no-commit-id", "--name-only", "-r", "-m", "--first-parent", sha).split("\n"):
    69	        if path and path not in seen:
    70	            listed.append({"path": path, "language": "Markdown" if path.endswith((".md", ".txt")) else "", "kind": "file", "name": path, "type": "M", "dependents": 0})
    71	    inside = [c for c in listed if c["path"].startswith(prefix)]
    72	    if not inside:
    73	        return ELSEWHERE, "never touched the agent's folder"
    74	    best, why = 0.0, ""
    75	    for change in inside:
    76	        short = change["path"][len(prefix):]
    77	        if change["language"] in DOC_LANGUAGES:
    78	            weight, reason = DOCS, f"only touched {short}, which the agent does not run"
    79	        elif change["language"] not in CODE_LANGUAGES:
    80	            weight, reason = DATA, f"changed {short}, a data or dependency file the graph cannot follow"
    81	        elif change["path"] == entry_path:
    82	            weight, reason = REACHES, f"changed {change['name'] if change['kind'] != 'module' else 'the body of ' + short}, in the agent's own file"
    83	        elif change["kind"] in ("module", "file"):
    84	            weight, reason = UNCALLED, f"changed {short}, a separate script"
    85	        else:
    86	            reached = called_from(repo, change["name"], change["path"], entry_path)
    87	            if reached is None:
    88	                weight, reason = UNKNOWN, f"changed {change['name']} in {short}, and the graph has no record of its callers"
    89	            elif reached:
    90	                weight, reason = REACHES, f"changed {change['name']} in {short}, which the agent calls"
    91	            else:
    92	                weight, reason = UNCALLED, f"changed {change['name']} in {short}, which the agent never calls"
    93	        if weight > best:
    94	            best, why = weight, reason
    95	    return best, why

     1	"""The suspects: every commit after the last good ref, up to and including the first bad one."""
     2	
     3	import subprocess
     4	from dataclasses import dataclass

     7	# A commit that never touched the agent's folder can still be guilty (a shared file, a
     8	# lockfile higher up), so it keeps a small prior. Plain bisect ignores priors.
     9	PRIOR_TOUCHES_TARGET = 1.0
    10	PRIOR_ELSEWHERE = 0.05
    11	
    12	
    13	@dataclass(frozen=True)
    14	class Suspect:
    15	    sha: str
    16	    subject: str
    17	    files: tuple[str, ...]
    18	    checkpoint: str | None  # Entire checkpoint id from the commit trailer
    19	    touches_target: bool
    20	    prior: float
    21	    alibi: str = ""  # why this commit starts with less suspicion, when entire-graph gives a reason
    22	
    23	    @property
    24	    def short(self) -> str:
    25	        return self.sha[:12]

    28	def git(repo: str | Path, *args: str) -> str:
    29	    done = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(repo), *args], capture_output=True, text=True)
    30	    if done.returncode != 0:
    31	        raise RuntimeError(f"git {' '.join(args)} failed: {done.stderr.strip()}")
    32	    return done.stdout

    39	def list_suspects(repo: str | Path, good: str, bad: str, target: str = ".", graph: bool = False) -> list[Suspect]:
    40	    """Commits in good..bad, oldest first. The last one is the bad ref itself.
    41	
    42	    The path filter gives the first prior: a commit that never touched the agent's folder keeps
    43	    a small one. With `graph`, entire-graph refines it for the commits that did, by asking
    44	    whether what they changed is something the agent runs.
    45	    """
    46	    shas = git(repo, "rev-list", "--reverse", "--ancestry-path", f"{good}..{bad}").split()
    47	    prefix = "" if target in (".", "") else target.rstrip("/") + "/"
    48	    suspects = []
    49	    for sha in shas:
    50	        subject, _, trailer = git(
    51	            repo, "show", "-s", "--format=%s%x00%(trailers:key=Entire-Checkpoint,valueonly,separator=%x20)", sha
    52	        ).strip().partition("\x00")
    53	        files = tuple(git(repo, "diff-tree", "--no-commit-id", "--name-only", "-r", "-m", "--first-parent", sha).split("\n"))
    54	        files = tuple(f for f in files if f)
    55	        touches = any(f.startswith(prefix) for f in files)
    56	        prior, alibi = (PRIOR_TOUCHES_TARGET, "") if touches else (PRIOR_ELSEWHERE, "never touched the agent's folder")
    57	        if graph and touches:
    58	            from .graph import alibi as graph_alibi  # imported here because graph.py uses git() from this module
    59	
    60	            prior, reason = graph_alibi(repo, sha, target)
    61	            alibi = reason if prior < 1.0 else ""
    62	        suspects.append(Suspect(
    63	            sha=sha, subject=subject, files=files, checkpoint=trailer.split()[0] if trailer.strip() else None,
    64	            touches_target=touches, prior=prior, alibi=alibi,
    65	        ))
    66	    return suspects

     1	"""The ruling: revert the culprit, or keep what it was for and patch it?
     2

     7	import json
     8	import re
     9	from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass
    10	from datetime import date
    11	from pathlib import Path
    12	
    13	REVERT, PATCH = "revert", "patch"
    14	
    15	KINDS = {
    16	    "prompt": "a change to the agent's instructions",
    17	    "model-settings": "a change to the model or its settings",
    18	    "dependency": "a dependency change",
    19	    "tool-code": "a change to the code of a tool the agent calls",
    20	    "agent-code": "a change to the agent's own code",
    21	    "other": "a change outside the agent's code",
    22	}
    23	
    24	
    25	@dataclass
    26	class Ruling:
    27	    kind: str
    28	    ruling: str  # revert or patch
    29	    decided_on: str
    30	    first_case: str
    31	    culprit: str
    32	    note: str = ""
    33	
    34	
    35	def classify(diff: str, files: list[str]) -> str:
    36	    """What kind of change the culprit made, from its diff. Rough on purpose: it only picks which standing ruling applies."""
    37	    changed = [line[1:] for line in diff.splitlines() if line[:1] in "+-" and not line.startswith(("+++", "---"))]
    38	    text = "\n".join(changed)
    39	    names = " ".join(files).lower()
    40	    if re.search(r"(pyproject\.toml|uv\.lock|requirements[\w.-]*\.txt|package(-lock)?\.json)", names) and not re.search(r"\.py\b", names):
    41	        return "dependency"
    42	    if re.search(r"\b(SYSTEM|PROMPT|INSTRUCTIONS)[A-Z_]*\b|system_prompt|\"role\": \"system\"", text) or "prompt" in names:
    43	        return "prompt"
    44	    # A reworded prompt often changes only the string lines inside it, and the name sits in the context.
    45	    only_strings = bool(changed) and all(line.strip()[:1] in "\"'#" or line.strip()[:2] in ('f"', "f'") for line in changed if line.strip())
    46	    if only_strings and re.search(r"\b(SYSTEM|PROMPT|INSTRUCTIONS)[A-Z_]*\b|system_prompt", diff):
    47	        return "prompt"
    48	    if re.search(r"\b(MODEL|temperature|max_tokens|top_p)\b", text):
    49	        return "model-settings"
    50	    # A tool's own lines are often context around the change, so this one reads the whole diff.
    51	    if re.search(r"kind=\"TOOL\"|\bTOOLS\b|def call_tool\b", diff):
    52	        return "tool-code"
    53	    if re.search(r"\.py\b", names):
    54	        return "agent-code"
    55	    return "other"

    57	
    58	def path_for(repo: str | Path, kind: str) -> Path:
    59	    return Path(repo) / "rulings" / f"{kind}.json"

    62	def recall(repo: str | Path, kind: str) -> Ruling | None:
    63	    path = path_for(repo, kind)
    64	    return Ruling(**json.loads(path.read_text())) if path.is_file() else None

    66	
    67	def question(kind: str, subject: str, request: str | None) -> str:
    68	    asked = f' It was asked for with: "{request.strip().splitlines()[0][:160]}"' if request else ""
    69	    return (
    70	        f"The culprit is {KINDS.get(kind, kind)}: \"{subject}\".{asked}\n"
    71	        f"Revert it, or keep what it was for and patch the bug? This answer becomes the rule for every {kind} case. [revert/patch] "
    72	    )
    73	
    74	
    75	def decide(repo: str | Path, kind: str, case_id: str, culprit: str, subject: str, request: str | None = None,
    76	           answer: str | None = None, ask=None) -> tuple[Ruling, bool]:
    77	    """Return (ruling, asked). Asks only when there is no ruling for this kind yet."""
    78	    known = recall(repo, kind)
    79	    if known:
    80	        return known, False
    81	    if answer is None:
    82	        answer = (ask or input)(question(kind, subject, request))
    83	    answer = answer.strip().lower()
    84	    if answer not in (REVERT, PATCH):
    85	        raise ValueError(f"the ruling has to be revert or patch, and was {answer!r}")
    86	    ruling = Ruling(kind=kind, ruling=answer, decided_on=date.today().isoformat(), first_case=case_id, culprit=culprit)

    88	    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    89	    path.write_text(json.dumps(asdict(ruling), indent=1) + "\n")

     1	"""Alibis from entire-graph: can this commit's changes reach the agent at all?
     2	
     3	`entire graph commit` lists what a commit changed as entities (a function, a module body, a
     4	document) and `entire graph impact` gives a symbol's callers. A commit that only touched the
     5	README, or a helper script the agent never calls, has an alibi and starts with less suspicion.
     6	It is never cleared outright: the lineup can still land on it if the replays say so.
     7	"""
     8	
     9	import json
    10	import subprocess
    11	from pathlib import Path
    12	
    13	from .suspects import git
    14	
    15	REACHES, UNKNOWN, DATA, UNCALLED, DOCS, ELSEWHERE = 1.0, 1.0, 0.6, 0.15, 0.05, 0.05
    16	DOC_LANGUAGES = {"Markdown", "Git Ignore", "Text", "HTML", "CSS"}
    17	CODE_LANGUAGES = {"Python", "TypeScript", "JavaScript", "Go", "Rust", "Java", "Ruby"}
    18	
    19	
    20	def _graph(repo: str | Path, *args: str, timeout: float = 120.0) -> dict | None:
    21	    """Run an entire-graph command that prints JSON. None if the plugin is missing or the call fails."""
    22	    try:
    23	        done = subprocess.run(["entire", "graph", *args], cwd=repo, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout)
    24	    except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired):
    25	        return None
    26	    if done.returncode != 0:
    27	        return None
    28	    try:
    29	        return json.loads(done.stdout)
    30	    except json.JSONDecodeError:
    31	        return None
    32	
    33	
    34	def changes(repo: str | Path, sha: str) -> list[dict] | None:
    35	    """What a commit changed, one entry per entity: {"path", "language", "kind", "name", "type", "dependents"}."""
    36	    found = _graph(repo, "commit", sha, "--json")
    37	    if found is None:
    38	        return None
    39	    out = []
    40	    for file in found.get("files") or []:
    41	        listed = file.get("changes") or [{"kind": "file", "name": file["path"], "type": file.get("status", "M")}]
    42	        for change in listed:
    43	            out.append({
    44	                "path": file["path"], "language": file.get("language") or "", "kind": change.get("kind", ""),
    45	                "name": change.get("name", ""), "type": change.get("type", ""), "dependents": change.get("dependents_count", 0),
    46	            })
    47	    return out
    48	
    49	
    50	def called_from(repo: str | Path, name: str, path: str, entry: str) -> bool | None:
    51	    """Is this symbol called, directly or through one other function, by code in the entry file? None if unknown."""
    52	    found = _graph(repo, "impact", "--symbol", name, "--file", path, "--repo", ".", "--depth", "2", "--limit", "60", "--format", "json", "--head")
    53	    if found is None or not found.get("focus") or found.get("disambiguation_required"):
    54	        return None
    55	    callers = [entry_["endpoint"].get("file_path", "") for entry_ in (found.get("callers") or {}).get("entries", [])]
    56	    return entry in callers
    57	
    58	
    59	def alibi(repo: str | Path, sha: str, target: str, entry: str = "agent.py") -> tuple[float, str]:
    60	    """(prior weight, reason) for one suspect. A weight of 1 means no alibi."""
    61	    prefix = "" if target in (".", "") else target.rstrip("/") + "/"
    62	    entry_path = prefix + entry
    63	    listed = changes(repo, sha)
    64	    if listed is None:
    65	        return UNKNOWN, "entire-graph could not read this commit"
    66	    # Files the graph does not parse (a lockfile, say) are missing from its list. Git knows them.
    67	    seen = {c["path"] for c in listed}
    68	    for path in git(repo, "diff-tree", "--no-commit-id", "--name-only", "-r", "-m", "--first-parent", sha).split("\n"):
    69	        if path and path not in seen:
    70	            listed.append({"path": path, "language": "Markdown" if path.endswith((".md", ".txt")) else "", "kind": "file", "name": path, "type": "M", "dependents": 0})
    71	    inside = [c for c in listed if c["path"].startswith(prefix)]
    72	    if not inside:
    73	        return ELSEWHERE, "never touched the agent's folder"
    74	    best, why = 0.0, ""
    75	    for change in inside:
    76	        short = change["path"][len(prefix):]
    77	        if change["language"] in DOC_LANGUAGES:
    78	            weight, reason = DOCS, f"only touched {short}, which the agent does not run"
    79	        elif change["language"] not in CODE_LANGUAGES:
    80	            weight, reason = DATA, f"changed {short}, a data or dependency file the graph cannot follow"
    81	        elif change["path"] == entry_path:
    82	            weight, reason = REACHES, f"changed {change['name'] if change['kind'] != 'module' else 'the body of ' + short}, in the agent's own file"
    83	        elif change["kind"] in ("module", "file"):
    84	            weight, reason = UNCALLED, f"changed {short}, a separate script"
    85	        else:
    86	            reached = called_from(repo, change["name"], change["path"], entry_path)
    87	            if reached is None:
    88	                weight, reason = UNKNOWN, f"changed {change['name']} in {short}, and the graph has no record of its callers"
    89	            elif reached:
    90	                weight, reason = REACHES, f"changed {change['name']} in {short}, which the agent calls"
    91	            else:
    92	                weight, reason = UNCALLED, f"changed {change['name']} in {short}, which the agent never calls"
    93	        if weight > best:
    94	            best, why = weight, reason
    95	    return best, why

    33	def traffic(mcp: Mcp, workflow: str, limit: int = 5000) -> list[dict]:
    34	    """The workflow's ordinary runs, oldest first, each with its commit. Whodunit's own replays are left out."""
    35	    safe = workflow.replace("'", "''")
    36	    rows = select_all(mcp, (
    37	        "select r.trace_id, r.started_ms, r.input_preview, s.output_preview as info, "
    38	        "(r.status = 'error' or r.error_count > 0 or r.finding_count > 0) as bad "
    39	        "from runs r join spans s on s.trace_id = r.trace_id and s.name = 'run_info' "
    40	        f"where r.workflow = '{safe}' and r.doctor = 0 and s.attributes not like '%case:%' order by r.started_ms"
    41	    ), cap=limit)
    42	    out = []
    43	    for row in rows:
    44	        try:
    45	            tags = json.loads(row.pop("info") or "{}").get("tags", [])
    46	        except (json.JSONDecodeError, AttributeError):
    47	            continue
    48	        commit = next((t.split(":", 1)[1] for t in tags if t.startswith("commit:")), None)
    49	        if commit and commit != "unknown":
    50	            out.append({**row, "commit": commit, "bad": bool(row["bad"])})

    54	def find_onset(workflow: str, runs: list[dict], floor: float = 0.01) -> Onset:
    55	    """Where the failures begin, given runs as {"commit", "started_ms", "bad", "input_preview"}, oldest first.
    56	
    57	    Commits are ordered by when they were first seen. The oldest commit is taken as the baseline.
    58	    The good ref is the last commit before the change point's posterior reaches `floor`, so the
    59	    range handed to the lineup is wide enough to hold the culprit.
    60	    """
    61	    order: dict[str, dict] = {}
    62	    for run in runs:
    63	        seen = order.setdefault(run["commit"], {"sha": run["commit"], "first_seen_ms": run["started_ms"], "runs": 0, "bad": 0})
    64	        seen["runs"] += 1
    65	        seen["bad"] += run["bad"]
    66	    commits = list(order.values())
    67	    onset = Onset(workflow=workflow, commits=commits, runs=len(runs), bad_runs=sum(r["bad"] for r in runs))
    68	    if len(commits) < 2:
    69	        onset.note = "Runs from at least two commits are needed to place the onset."
    70	        return onset
    71	    if onset.bad_runs == 0:
    72	        onset.note = "No bad runs in the traffic."
    73	        return onset
    74	    state = ChangePoint(len(commits) - 1)  # the oldest commit plays the good ref
    75	    for position, commit in enumerate(commits):
    76	        for _ in range(commit["bad"]):
    77	            state.observe(position - 1, True)
    78	        for _ in range(commit["runs"] - commit["bad"]):
    79	            state.observe(position - 1, False)
    80	    posterior = state.posterior()
    81	    top = max(range(len(posterior)), key=posterior.__getitem__)
    82	    mass, start = 0.0, 0
    83	    for i, share in enumerate(posterior):
    84	        mass += share
    85	        if mass >= floor:
    86	            start = i
    87	            break
    88	    onset.good = commits[start]["sha"]  # suspect i is commits[i + 1], so the commit before suspect `start` is commits[start]
    89	    onset.bad = commits[-1]["sha"]
    90	    onset.likeliest, onset.probability = commits[top + 1]["sha"], round(posterior[top], 4)
    91	    since = commits[top + 1]["first_seen_ms"]
    92	    later_bad = [r for r in runs if r["bad"] and r["started_ms"] >= since]
    93	    onset.first_failure_ms = later_bad[0]["started_ms"] if later_bad else None
    94	    inputs: dict[str, int] = {}
    95	    for run in later_bad:
    96	        if run.get("input_preview"):
    97	            inputs[run["input_preview"]] = inputs.get(run["input_preview"], 0) + 1
    98	    onset.failing_inputs = sorted(inputs, key=lambda text: -inputs[text])[:5]
    99	    return onset

   123	def witness(mcp: Mcp, workflow: str, positions: dict[str, int], inputs: list[tuple[str, list[dict]]]) -> list[tuple[int, bool]]:
   124	    """What ordinary traffic already says about a case, as (position, failed) pairs for the lineup.
   125	
   126	    `positions` maps a commit to its place in the lineup (-1 for the good ref). A run counts when
   127	    it asked exactly what one of the case's inputs asks, and it failed if what it refunded is not
   128	    what the case expects. These runs were already paid for, so they cost the lineup nothing.
   129	    """
   130	    expected = {text: {str(r["order_id"]): float(r["refunded"]) for r in refunds} for text, refunds in inputs}
   131	    safe = workflow.replace("'", "''")
   132	    asked = ", ".join("'" + text.replace("'", "''") + "'" for text in expected) or "''"
   133	    rows = select_all(mcp, (
   134	        "select r.trace_id, r.input_preview, s.output_preview as info from runs r "
   135	        "join spans s on s.trace_id = r.trace_id and s.name = 'run_info' "
   136	        f"where r.workflow = '{safe}' and r.doctor = 0 and r.input_preview in ({asked}) and s.attributes not like '%case:%' "
   137	        "order by r.started_ms desc"
   138	    ), cap=1000)
   139	    runs = []
   140	    for row in rows:
   141	        try:
   142	            tags = json.loads(row["info"] or "{}").get("tags", [])
   143	        except (json.JSONDecodeError, AttributeError):
   144	            continue
   145	        commit = next((t.split(":", 1)[1] for t in tags if t.startswith("commit:")), None)
   146	        if commit in positions:
   147	            runs.append((row["trace_id"], row["input_preview"], positions[commit]))
   148	    if not runs:
   149	        return []
   150	    ids = ", ".join("'" + trace + "'" for trace, _, _ in runs)
   151	    paid: dict[str, dict[str, float]] = {trace: {} for trace, _, _ in runs}
   152	    for span in select_all(mcp, f"select trace_id, output_preview from spans where name = 'issue_refund' and status_code != 2 and trace_id in ({ids})"):
   153	        try:
   154	            out = json.loads(span["output_preview"] or "{}")
   155	            order, amount = str(out["order_id"]), float(out["refunded"])
   156	        except (json.JSONDecodeError, KeyError, TypeError, ValueError):
   157	            continue
   158	        paid[span["trace_id"]][order] = paid[span["trace_id"]].get(order, 0.0) + amount
   159	    evidence = []
   160	    for trace, text, position in runs:
   161	        want, got = expected[text], paid[trace]
   162	        wrong = any(abs(got.get(o, 0.0) - want.get(o, 0.0)) > 0.005 for o in set(got) | set(want))
   163	        evidence.append((position, wrong))
   164	    return evidence

     1	"""A simulator for the lineup: how often is the right commit named, for a given replay budget?
     2	
     3	    python -m whodunit.simulate --out eval/simulator
     4	
     5	Each simulated case has `suspects` commits and one culprit chosen at random. A commit before
     6	the culprit fails at `good_rate`, and the culprit and everything after it fails at `bad_rate`.
     7	Three methods get the same case and the same budget of replays:
     8	
     9	- statistical: the statistical bisect in whodunit.lineup.
    10	- plain, repeated: plain bisect that replays each commit up to k times and calls it bad on the
    11	  first failure, with k as large as the budget allows.
    12	- plain, once: plain bisect with one replay per commit, which is what `git bisect run` does.
    13	"""
    14	
    15	import argparse
    16	import json
    17	import math
    18	import random
    19	from concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor
    20	from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass
    21	from pathlib import Path
    22	
    23	from .lineup import FAIL, PASS, plain_bisect, statistical_bisect
    24	
    25	RATES = (1.0, 0.8, 0.6, 0.4, 0.3, 0.2)
    26	BUDGETS = (10, 20, 30, 40, 60, 80, 120, 160, 240, 320)
    27	METHODS = ("statistical", "plain_repeated", "plain_once")
    28	
    29	
    30	@dataclass
    31	class Cell:
    32	    method: str
    33	    bad_rate: float
    34	    good_rate: float
    35	    budget: int
    36	    suspects: int
    37	    trials: int
    38	    right: int = 0
    39	    wrong: int = 0
    40	    nobody: int = 0
    41	    top_right: int = 0  # the most likely suspect was the culprit, whether or not anyone was named
    42	    replays: int = 0  # total over all trials
    43	
    44	    @property
    45	    def accuracy(self) -> float:
    46	        return self.right / self.trials
    47	
    48	
    49	def one_case(method: str, suspects: int, culprit: int, bad_rate: float, good_rate: float, budget: int, rng: random.Random):
    50	    """Returns (accused index or None, most likely suspect or None, replays used)."""
    51	    used = 0
    52	
    53	    def trial(position: int) -> str:
    54	        nonlocal used
    55	        used += 1
    56	        return FAIL if rng.random() < (bad_rate if position >= culprit else good_rate) else PASS
    57	
    58	    if method == "statistical":
    59	        found = statistical_bisect(suspects, trial, budget)
    60	        return found.culprit, None if found.note else found.remaining[0], found.replays
    61	    steps = max(1, math.ceil(math.log2(suspects)))
    62	    repeats = 1 if method == "plain_once" else max(1, budget // steps)
    63	
    64	    def test(index: int) -> str:
    65	        for _ in range(repeats):
    66	            if trial(index) == FAIL:
    67	                return FAIL
    68	        return PASS
    69	
    70	    accused = plain_bisect(suspects, test).culprit
    71	    return accused, accused, used
    72	
    73	
    74	def run_cell(cell: Cell, seed: int = 0) -> Cell:
    75	    for n in range(cell.trials):
    76	        # The culprit depends on the trial alone, so every method and budget meets the same cases.
    77	        culprit = random.Random(f"culprit-{seed}-{n}").randrange(cell.suspects)
    78	        rng = random.Random(f"{seed}-{cell.method}-{cell.bad_rate}-{cell.good_rate}-{cell.budget}-{n}")
    79	        accused, top, used = one_case(cell.method, cell.suspects, culprit, cell.bad_rate, cell.good_rate, cell.budget, rng)
    80	        cell.replays += used
    81	        cell.top_right += top == culprit
    82	        if accused is None:
    83	            cell.nobody += 1
    84	        elif accused == culprit:
    85	            cell.right += 1
    86	        else:
    87	            cell.wrong += 1
    88	    return cell
    89	
    90	
    91	def sweep(suspects: int = 40, trials: int = 500, good_rate: float = 0.0, rates=RATES, budgets=BUDGETS, workers: int | None = None) -> list[Cell]:
    92	    cells = [Cell(m, r, good_rate, b, suspects, trials) for r in rates for b in budgets for m in METHODS]
    93	    with ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=workers) as pool:
    94	        return list(pool.map(run_cell, cells, chunksize=4))
    95	
    96	
    97	def to_rows(cells: list[Cell]) -> list[dict]:
    98	    return [{**asdict(c), "accuracy": round(c.accuracy, 4), "mean_replays": round(c.replays / c.trials, 1)} for c in cells]
    99	
   100	
   101	def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
   102	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
   103	    parser.add_argument("--out", default="eval/simulator")
   104	    parser.add_argument("--suspects", type=int, default=40)
   105	    parser.add_argument("--trials", type=int, default=500)
   106	    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
   107	    out = Path(args.out)
   108	    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   109	    results = {}
   110	    for name, good_rate in (("clean_baseline", 0.0), ("flaky_baseline", 0.05)):
   111	        rows = to_rows(sweep(args.suspects, args.trials, good_rate))
   112	        results[name] = {"suspects": args.suspects, "trials": args.trials, "good_rate": good_rate, "cells": rows}
   113	        print(f"{name}: {len(rows)} cells")
   114	    (out / "results.json").write_text(json.dumps(results, indent=1) + "\n")
   115	    from .chart import write_charts
   116	
   117	    write_charts(results, out)
   118	    return 0
   119	
   120	
   121	if __name__ == "__main__":
   122	    raise SystemExit(main())

     1	"""The onset: when did the failures begin, and between which commits?
     2	
     3	Every run of the agent carries the commit it ran on. Ordinary traffic therefore already says
     4	a good deal about the culprit before any replay is spent: this module reads those runs from
     5	neatroots, and uses the same change-point model as the lineup to find where the failures start.
     6	"""
     7	
     8	import json
     9	from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field
    10	
    11	from .lineup import ChangePoint
    12	from .neat import Mcp, select_all

    15	@dataclass
    16	class Onset:
    17	    workflow: str
    18	    commits: list[dict]  # in order of first appearance: {"sha", "first_seen_ms", "runs", "bad"}
    19	    good: str | None = None  # last commit that is very unlikely to be at or after the change
    20	    bad: str | None = None  # newest commit seen
    21	    likeliest: str | None = None  # the single most likely first bad commit, from traffic alone
    22	    probability: float = 0.0
    23	    first_failure_ms: float | None = None  # first bad run at or after the likeliest commit
    24	    bad_runs: int = 0
    25	    runs: int = 0
    26	    failing_inputs: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    27	    note: str = ""
    28	
    29	    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
    30	        return asdict(self)
    31	
    32	
    33	def traffic(mcp: Mcp, workflow: str, limit: int = 5000) -> list[dict]:
    34	    """The workflow's ordinary runs, oldest first, each with its commit. Whodunit's own replays are left out."""
    35	    safe = workflow.replace("'", "''")
    36	    rows = select_all(mcp, (
    37	        "select r.trace_id, r.started_ms, r.input_preview, s.output_preview as info, "
    38	        "(r.status = 'error' or r.error_count > 0 or r.finding_count > 0) as bad "
    39	        "from runs r join spans s on s.trace_id = r.trace_id and s.name = 'run_info' "
    40	        f"where r.workflow = '{safe}' and r.doctor = 0 and s.attributes not like '%case:%' order by r.started_ms"
    41	    ), cap=limit)
    42	    out = []
    43	    for row in rows:
    44	        try:
    45	            tags = json.loads(row.pop("info") or "{}").get("tags", [])
    46	        except (json.JSONDecodeError, AttributeError):
    47	            continue
    48	        commit = next((t.split(":", 1)[1] for t in tags if t.startswith("commit:")), None)
    49	        if commit and commit != "unknown":
    50	            out.append({**row, "commit": commit, "bad": bool(row["bad"])})
    51	    return out
    52	
    53	
    54	def find_onset(workflow: str, runs: list[dict], floor: float = 0.01) -> Onset:
    55	    """Where the failures begin, given runs as {"commit", "started_ms", "bad", "input_preview"}, oldest first.
    56	
    57	    Commits are ordered by when they were first seen. The oldest commit is taken as the baseline.
    58	    The good ref is the last commit before the change point's posterior reaches `floor`, so the
    59	    range handed to the lineup is wide enough to hold the culprit.
    60	    """
    61	    order: dict[str, dict] = {}
    62	    for run in runs:
    63	        seen = order.setdefault(run["commit"], {"sha": run["commit"], "first_seen_ms": run["started_ms"], "runs": 0, "bad": 0})
    64	        seen["runs"] += 1
    65	        seen["bad"] += run["bad"]
    66	    commits = list(order.values())
    67	    onset = Onset(workflow=workflow, commits=commits, runs=len(runs), bad_runs=sum(r["bad"] for r in runs))
    68	    if len(commits) < 2:
    69	        onset.note = "Runs from at least two commits are needed to place the onset."
    70	        return onset
    71	    if onset.bad_runs == 0:
    72	        onset.note = "No bad runs in the traffic."
    73	        return onset
    74	    state = ChangePoint(len(commits) - 1)  # the oldest commit plays the good ref
    75	    for position, commit in enumerate(commits):
    76	        for _ in range(commit["bad"]):
    77	            state.observe(position - 1, True)
    78	        for _ in range(commit["runs"] - commit["bad"]):
    79	            state.observe(position - 1, False)
    80	    posterior = state.posterior()
    81	    top = max(range(len(posterior)), key=posterior.__getitem__)
    82	    mass, start = 0.0, 0
    83	    for i, share in enumerate(posterior):
    84	        mass += share
    85	        if mass >= floor:
    86	            start = i
    87	            break
    88	    onset.good = commits[start]["sha"]  # suspect i is commits[i + 1], so the commit before suspect `start` is commits[start]
    89	    onset.bad = commits[-1]["sha"]
    90	    onset.likeliest, onset.probability = commits[top + 1]["sha"], round(posterior[top], 4)
    91	    since = commits[top + 1]["first_seen_ms"]
    92	    later_bad = [r for r in runs if r["bad"] and r["started_ms"] >= since]
    93	    onset.first_failure_ms = later_bad[0]["started_ms"] if later_bad else None
    94	    inputs: dict[str, int] = {}
    95	    for run in later_bad:
    96	        if run.get("input_preview"):
    97	            inputs[run["input_preview"]] = inputs.get(run["input_preview"], 0) + 1
    98	    onset.failing_inputs = sorted(inputs, key=lambda text: -inputs[text])[:5]
    99	    return onset

   102	def cloud_trend(detection: str = "Execution Failed") -> dict:
   103	    """Ask neatlogs cloud when a detection started firing. Needs NEATLOGS_API_KEY in .env.
   104	
   105	    Returns {"detection", "first_seen", "total", "points"}, where first_seen is the start of the
   106	    first bucket with any occurrences, or None if the detection has not fired in the period.
   107	    """

   109	
   110	    from .env import load_env
   111	    from .neat import NEATLOGS
   112	
   113	    load_env()
   114	    key = os.environ.get("NEATLOGS_API_KEY", "")
   115	    if not key:
   116	        raise RuntimeError("NEATLOGS_API_KEY is not in .env")
   117	    trend = Mcp(NEATLOGS, token=key).call("get_detection_trend", detection_name=detection)
   118	    points = trend.get("data_points", [])
   119	    first = next((p["date"] for p in points if p.get("count", 0) > 0), None)
   120	    return {"detection": trend.get("detection_name", detection), "first_seen": first, "total": trend.get("total_occurrences", 0), "points": points}

   123	def witness(mcp: Mcp, workflow: str, positions: dict[str, int], inputs: list[tuple[str, list[dict]]]) -> list[tuple[int, bool]]:
   124	    """What ordinary traffic already says about a case, as (position, failed) pairs for the lineup.
   125	
   126	    `positions` maps a commit to its place in the lineup (-1 for the good ref). A run counts when
   127	    it asked exactly what one of the case's inputs asks, and it failed if what it refunded is not
   128	    what the case expects. These runs were already paid for, so they cost the lineup nothing.
   129	    """
   130	    expected = {text: {str(r["order_id"]): float(r["refunded"]) for r in refunds} for text, refunds in inputs}
   131	    safe = workflow.replace("'", "''")
   132	    asked = ", ".join("'" + text.replace("'", "''") + "'" for text in expected) or "''"
   133	    rows = select_all(mcp, (
   134	        "select r.trace_id, r.input_preview, s.output_preview as info from runs r "
   135	        "join spans s on s.trace_id = r.trace_id and s.name = 'run_info' "
   136	        f"where r.workflow = '{safe}' and r.doctor = 0 and r.input_preview in ({asked}) and s.attributes not like '%case:%' "
   137	        "order by r.started_ms desc"
   138	    ), cap=1000)
   139	    runs = []
   140	    for row in rows:
   141	        try:
   142	            tags = json.loads(row["info"] or "{}").get("tags", [])
   143	        except (json.JSONDecodeError, AttributeError):
   144	            continue
   145	        commit = next((t.split(":", 1)[1] for t in tags if t.startswith("commit:")), None)
   146	        if commit in positions:
   147	            runs.append((row["trace_id"], row["input_preview"], positions[commit]))
   148	    if not runs:
   149	        return []
   150	    ids = ", ".join("'" + trace + "'" for trace, _, _ in runs)
   151	    paid: dict[str, dict[str, float]] = {trace: {} for trace, _, _ in runs}
   152	    for span in select_all(mcp, f"select trace_id, output_preview from spans where name = 'issue_refund' and status_code != 2 and trace_id in ({ids})"):
   153	        try:
   154	            out = json.loads(span["output_preview"] or "{}")
   155	            order, amount = str(out["order_id"]), float(out["refunded"])
   156	        except (json.JSONDecodeError, KeyError, TypeError, ValueError):
   157	            continue
   158	        paid[span["trace_id"]][order] = paid[span["trace_id"]].get(order, 0.0) + amount
   159	    evidence = []
   160	    for trace, text, position in runs:
   161	        want, got = expected[text], paid[trace]
   162	        wrong = any(abs(got.get(o, 0.0) - want.get(o, 0.0)) > 0.005 for o in set(got) | set(want))

     1	"""A simulator for the lineup: how often is the right commit named, for a given replay budget?
     2	
     3	    python -m whodunit.simulate --out eval/simulator
     4	
     5	Each simulated case has `suspects` commits and one culprit chosen at random. A commit before
     6	the culprit fails at `good_rate`, and the culprit and everything after it fails at `bad_rate`.
     7	Three methods get the same case and the same budget of replays:
     8	
     9	- statistical: the statistical bisect in whodunit.lineup.
    10	- plain, repeated: plain bisect that replays each commit up to k times and calls it bad on the
    11	  first failure, with k as large as the budget allows.
    12	- plain, once: plain bisect with one replay per commit, which is what `git bisect run` does.
    13	"""
    14	
    15	import argparse
    16	import json
    17	import math
    18	import random
    19	from concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor
    20	from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass
    21	from pathlib import Path
    22	
    23	from .lineup import FAIL, PASS, plain_bisect, statistical_bisect
    24	
    25	RATES = (1.0, 0.8, 0.6, 0.4, 0.3, 0.2)
    26	BUDGETS = (10, 20, 30, 40, 60, 80, 120, 160, 240, 320)
    27	METHODS = ("statistical", "plain_repeated", "plain_once")
    28	
    29	
    30	@dataclass
    31	class Cell:
    32	    method: str
    33	    bad_rate: float
    34	    good_rate: float
    35	    budget: int
    36	    suspects: int
    37	    trials: int
    38	    right: int = 0
    39	    wrong: int = 0
    40	    nobody: int = 0
    41	    top_right: int = 0  # the most likely suspect was the culprit, whether or not anyone was named
    42	    replays: int = 0  # total over all trials
    43	
    44	    @property
    45	    def accuracy(self) -> float:
    46	        return self.right / self.trials
    47	
    48	
    49	def one_case(method: str, suspects: int, culprit: int, bad_rate: float, good_rate: float, budget: int, rng: random.Random):
    50	    """Returns (accused index or None, most likely suspect or None, replays used)."""
    51	    used = 0
    52	
    53	    def trial(position: int) -> str:
    54	        nonlocal used
    55	        used += 1
    56	        return FAIL if rng.random() < (bad_rate if position >= culprit else good_rate) else PASS
    57	
    58	    if method == "statistical":
    59	        found = statistical_bisect(suspects, trial, budget)
    60	        return found.culprit, None if found.note else found.remaining[0], found.replays
    61	    steps = max(1, math.ceil(math.log2(suspects)))
    62	    repeats = 1 if method == "plain_once" else max(1, budget // steps)
    63	
    64	    def test(index: int) -> str:
    65	        for _ in range(repeats):
    66	            if trial(index) == FAIL:
    67	                return FAIL
    68	        return PASS
    69	
    70	    accused = plain_bisect(suspects, test).culprit
    71	    return accused, accused, used
    72	
    73	
    74	def run_cell(cell: Cell, seed: int = 0) -> Cell:
    75	    for n in range(cell.trials):
    76	        # The culprit depends on the trial alone, so every method and budget meets the same cases.
    77	        culprit = random.Random(f"culprit-{seed}-{n}").randrange(cell.suspects)
    78	        rng = random.Random(f"{seed}-{cell.method}-{cell.bad_rate}-{cell.good_rate}-{cell.budget}-{n}")
    79	        accused, top, used = one_case(cell.method, cell.suspects, culprit, cell.bad_rate, cell.good_rate, cell.budget, rng)
    80	        cell.replays += used
    81	        cell.top_right += top == culprit
    82	        if accused is None:
    83	            cell.nobody += 1
    84	        elif accused == culprit:
    85	            cell.right += 1
    86	        else:
    87	            cell.wrong += 1
    88	    return cell
    89	
    90	
    91	def sweep(suspects: int = 40, trials: int = 500, good_rate: float = 0.0, rates=RATES, budgets=BUDGETS, workers: int | None = None) -> list[Cell]:
    92	    cells = [Cell(m, r, good_rate, b, suspects, trials) for r in rates for b in budgets for m in METHODS]
    93	    with ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=workers) as pool:
    94	        return list(pool.map(run_cell, cells, chunksize=4))
    95	
    96	
    97	def to_rows(cells: list[Cell]) -> list[dict]:
    98	    return [{**asdict(c), "accuracy": round(c.accuracy, 4), "mean_replays": round(c.replays / c.trials, 1)} for c in cells]
    99	
   100	
   101	def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
   102	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
   103	    parser.add_argument("--out", default="eval/simulator")
   104	    parser.add_argument("--suspects", type=int, default=40)
   105	    parser.add_argument("--trials", type=int, default=500)
   106	    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
   107	    out = Path(args.out)
   108	    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   109	    results = {}
   110	    for name, good_rate in (("clean_baseline", 0.0), ("flaky_baseline", 0.05)):
   111	        rows = to_rows(sweep(args.suspects, args.trials, good_rate))
   112	        results[name] = {"suspects": args.suspects, "trials": args.trials, "good_rate": good_rate, "cells": rows}
   113	        print(f"{name}: {len(rows)} cells")
   114	    (out / "results.json").write_text(json.dumps(results, indent=1) + "\n")
   115	    from .chart import write_charts
   116	
   117	    write_charts(results, out)
   118	    return 0
   119	
   120	
   121	if __name__ == "__main__":
   122	    raise SystemExit(main())

     1	# Whodunit

     3	41 commits since it last worked. Which one did it?
     4	
     5	Whodunit answers two questions about an AI agent that used to work and now fails: which commit broke it, and why that commit was made. Then it fixes the commit, proves the fix by replaying the failures, and counts what the breakage cost.
     6	
     7	It was built for neatHack between 10 and 12 October 2026. `hackathon.md` is the dated build log, including the parts that went wrong.
     8	
     9	## Why plain bisect is not enough
    10	
    11	`git bisect` assumes a bad commit fails every time. Agents do not behave that way. A prompt change might break one run in three, and a commit that is perfectly fine might still fail one run in twenty. Test a bad commit once, see it pass, and bisect walks off in the wrong direction without telling you.
    12	
    13	Whodunit replays the failing inputs against suspect commits and keeps a probability for each suspect being the first bad one. It names a commit only when it is 95% sure. If the replay budget runs out first, it hands back the suspects still in the lineup with their probabilities.
    14	
    15	How well that works is measured two ways. [eval/sealed](eval/sealed/README.md) is five regressions planted by a separate session with a sealed answer key: three were named inside 120 replays, all five after more, and no commit was wrongly accused. Plain bisect with five retries, on the same five, got three right with fewer replays, named an innocent commit on the fourth and could not start on the fifth. [eval/simulator](eval/simulator/README.md) is simulated cases with a known culprit. The short version: when good commits never fail, plain bisect with repeats is cheaper. When good commits fail 5% of the time on their own, it falls apart and the statistical bisect does not.
    16	
    17	## How a case runs
    18	
    19	A case is a small TOML file: a symptom, the failing inputs with what each should have produced, the last good ref and the first bad ref. One command runs all of it:
    20	
    21	```bash
    22	uv run whodunit investigate cases/whole-history.toml --from-traffic refund-agent
    23	```
    24	
    25	It stops only when it needs the owner's ruling. Each step is also a command of its own (`lineup`, `brief`, `ruling`, `fix`, `damages`, `open-case`), and each adds to one record next to the case file. The case file page is drawn from that record.
    26	
    27	On the refund agent's real history, 57 commits grown by a separate coding session, that command named the culprit at 99.8% after 20 replays, quoted the request that caused it, patched it, proved the patch on 30 clean replays and counted 120.00 in refunds that had gone to the wrong people. [evidence/casefile-whole-history.png](evidence/casefile-whole-history.png) is the page it wrote.
    28	
    29	0. Before any replay, two things narrow the field. entire-graph says which commits could not have reached the agent (a README edit, a helper script the agent never calls), and those start with less suspicion. And ordinary runs that already asked what the case asks are evidence that is already paid for.
    30	1. The lineup checks every suspect commit out into its own git worktree and replays the case inputs there. Each replay is a real run of the agent, traced to neatroots and tagged with the commit and the case. A commit that will not build is skipped, as `git bisect skip` does.
    31	2. The motive comes from Entire. A commit made by a coding agent carries a checkpoint, and the checkpoint holds the session. Whodunit finds the prompt that led to the commit and what the coding agent did next.
    32	3. The brief is written by a model from the culprit's diff, that slice of the session, and a failing run set against a passing one. Every sentence has to cite a span, a commit or a checkpoint that is really in the evidence. Sentences that do not are cut.
    33	4. The ruling is the owner's. It is asked once per kind of change (a prompt change, a tool change, a dependency) and remembered under `rulings/`.
    34	5. The fix is a revert or a patch on a local branch. It is proven only when its failure rate is back within 5 points of the rate before the culprit, at 95%, which takes about 30 clean replays. A patch that is not proven is tried once more with its failures in view, and after that the culprit is reverted. The case is kept under `cases/` as a regression test that `whodunit check` can replay against any ref.
    35	6. The damages are counted from the traces: how many runs went bad since the culprit, what they cost in tokens, and what they cost the shop, read from the refund tool's spans.
    36	
    37	Whodunit never pushes, opens a pull request or writes to anyone's finance model by itself. Those stay with the owner.
    38	
    39	## Try it
    40	
    41	You need Python 3.12, [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), git and a running neatroots.
    42	
    43	```bash
    44	uv sync
    45	uv run pytest -m "not slow"                    # the fast tests, no model and no keys
    46	
    47	# A throwaway repo with 20 commits, the refund agent and a planted bug:
    48	uv run python tests/planted.py /tmp/planted
    49	uv run python victims/refund-agent/fake_llm.py &
    50	uv run whodunit lineup /tmp/planted/case.toml --repo /tmp/planted --method plain
    51	```
    52	
    53	Add `flaky-lookup 40 27` to the `planted.py` line for 40 commits with a bug at commit 27 that fails about one run in three, and drop `--method plain` to use the statistical bisect.
    54	
    55	`uv run python -m whodunit.simulate --out eval/simulator` regenerates the simulator charts, and `uv run whodunit casebook` rewrites every case file and the index at `cases/index.html`.
    56	
    57	## What is in here
    58	
    59	- `whodunit/` is the tool. `lineup.py` holds both bisects, `replay.py` the worktree runner, `motive.py` the Entire lookups, `brief.py` the evidence and the brief, `ruling.py`, `fix.py` and `damages.py` the closing steps, and `casefile/` the page.
    60	- `victims/refund-agent/` is the agent under investigation. It started as the `refund-agent` example that ships with neatroots, which is licensed under Apache-2.0. The licence is in that folder and the changes are listed in its README.
    61	- `eval/simulator/` has the accuracy curves, the tables behind them and what they show.
    62	- `tests/planted.py` builds histories with a known culprit. The tests and the demo use the same builder.
    63	- `AGENTS.md` is the working brief for anyone writing code here.
    64	
    65	## Models and keys
    66	
    67	Keys live in `.env`, which git ignores. `.env.example` lists them. The code that needs a key reads the file itself.
    68	
    69	Replays of the refund agent use a scripted model by default and cost nothing. `REFUND_LLM=gateway` or `REFUND_LLM=own` switches them to a real model. Keep one model for the whole of a case, because a model change in the middle would look like a regression.
    70	
    71	The brief and the patch use `WHODUNIT_LLM`: `gateway`, `own`, `agent` for a coding agent in headless mode, or `none` for a fixed template with no model.
    72	
    73	## What it does not do yet
    74	
    75	- The statistical bisect assumes one change point. Two regressions in the same range will confuse it.
    76	- A replay that times out counts as a failure, so a badly overloaded machine can frame an innocent commit.
    77	- Damages are estimates from token counts and list prices.

    81	- About one coding session in nine lost its Entire checkpoint while the history was grown. For those commits the motive falls back to the commit message.

    13	Whodunit replays the failing inputs against suspect commits and keeps a probability for each suspect being the first bad one. It names a commit only when it is 95% sure. If the replay budget runs out first, it hands back the suspects still in the lineup with their probabilities.
    14	
    15	How well that works is measured two ways. [eval/sealed](eval/sealed/README.md) is five regressions planted by a separate session with a sealed answer key: three were named inside 120 replays, all five after more, and no commit was wrongly accused. Plain bisect with five retries, on the same five, got three right with fewer replays, named an innocent commit on the fourth and could not start on the fifth. [eval/simulator](eval/simulator/README.md) is simulated cases with a known culprit. The short version: when good commits never fail, plain bisect with repeats is cheaper. When good commits fail 5% of the time on their own, it falls apart and the statistical bisect does not.
    16	
    17	## How a case runs
    18	
    19	A case is a small TOML file: a symptom, the failing inputs with what each should have produced, the last good ref and the first bad ref. One command runs all of it:
    20	
    21	```bash
    22	uv run whodunit investigate cases/whole-history.toml --from-traffic refund-agent
    23	```
    24	
    25	It stops only when it needs the owner's ruling. Each step is also a command of its own (`lineup`, `brief`, `ruling`, `fix`, `damages`, `open-case`), and each adds to one record next to the case file. The case file page is drawn from that record.
    26	
    27	On the refund agent's real history, 57 commits grown by a separate coding session, that command named the culprit at 99.8% after 20 replays, quoted the request that caused it, patched it, proved the patch on 30 clean replays and counted 120.00 in refunds that had gone to the wrong people. [evidence/casefile-whole-history.png](evidence/casefile-whole-history.png) is the page it wrote.
    28	
    29	0. Before any replay, two things narrow the field. entire-graph says which commits could not have reached the agent (a README edit, a helper script the agent never calls), and those start with less suspicion. And ordinary runs that already asked what the case asks are evidence that is already paid for.
    30	1. The lineup checks every suspect commit out into its own git worktree and replays the case inputs there. Each replay is a real run of the agent, traced to neatroots and tagged with the commit and the case. A commit that will not build is skipped, as `git bisect skip` does.
    31	2. The motive comes from Entire. A commit made by a coding agent carries a checkpoint, and the checkpoint holds the session. Whodunit finds the prompt that led to the commit and what the coding agent did next.
    32	3. The brief is written by a model from the culprit's diff, that slice of the session, and a failing run set against a passing one. Every sentence has to cite a span, a commit or a checkpoint that is really in the evidence. Sentences that do not are cut.
    33	4. The ruling is the owner's. It is asked once per kind of change (a prompt change, a tool change, a dependency) and remembered under `rulings/`.
    34	5. The fix is a revert or a patch on a local branch. It is proven only when its failure rate is back within 5 points of the rate before the culprit, at 95%, which takes about 30 clean replays. A patch that is not proven is tried once more with its failures in view, and after that the culprit is reverted. The case is kept under `cases/` as a regression test that `whodunit check` can replay against any ref.
    35	6. The damages are counted from the traces: how many runs went bad since the culprit, what they cost in tokens, and what they cost the shop, read from the refund tool's spans.
    36	
    37	Whodunit never pushes, opens a pull request or writes to anyone's finance model by itself. Those stay with the owner.
    38	
    39	## Try it
    40	
    41	You need Python 3.12, [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), git and a running neatroots.
    42	
    43	```bash
    44	uv sync
    45	uv run pytest -m "not slow"                    # the fast tests, no model and no keys
    46	
    47	# A throwaway repo with 20 commits, the refund agent and a planted bug:
    48	uv run python tests/planted.py /tmp/planted
    49	uv run python victims/refund-agent/fake_llm.py &
    50	uv run whodunit lineup /tmp/planted/case.toml --repo /tmp/planted --method plain
    51	```

    54	
    55	`uv run python -m whodunit.simulate --out eval/simulator` regenerates the simulator charts, and `uv run whodunit casebook` rewrites every case file and the index at `cases/index.html`.
    56	
    57	## What is in here
    58	
    59	- `whodunit/` is the tool. `lineup.py` holds both bisects, `replay.py` the worktree runner, `motive.py` the Entire lookups, `brief.py` the evidence and the brief, `ruling.py`, `fix.py` and `damages.py` the closing steps, and `casefile/` the page.
    60	- `victims/refund-agent/` is the agent under investigation. It started as the `refund-agent` example that ships with neatroots, which is licensed under Apache-2.0. The licence is in that folder and the changes are listed in its README.
    61	- `eval/simulator/` has the accuracy curves, the tables behind them and what they show.
    62	- `tests/planted.py` builds histories with a known culprit. The tests and the demo use the same builder.
    63	- `AGENTS.md` is the working brief for anyone writing code here.
    64	
    65	## Models and keys
    66	
    67	Keys live in `.env`, which git ignores. `.env.example` lists them. The code that needs a key reads the file itself.

    69	Replays of the refund agent use a scripted model by default and cost nothing. `REFUND_LLM=gateway` or `REFUND_LLM=own` switches them to a real model. Keep one model for the whole of a case, because a model change in the middle would look like a regression.
    70	
    71	The brief and the patch use `WHODUNIT_LLM`: `gateway`, `own`, `agent` for a coding agent in headless mode, or `none` for a fixed template with no model.

---- eval/simulator/README.md
     1	# Simulator results
     2	
     3	How often does the lineup name the right commit, for a given number of replays? This folder answers that with simulated cases, where the culprit is known.
     4	
     5	Each case has 40 suspect commits and one culprit picked at random. Every point is 500 cases. Three methods get the same cases and the same replay budget:
     6	
     7	- The statistical bisect in `whodunit/lineup.py`. It names a commit only when it is 95% sure, and otherwise hands back the suspects that remain with their probabilities.
     8	- Plain bisect with repeats. It replays each commit as many times as the budget allows and calls the commit bad on the first failure.
     9	- Plain bisect with one replay per commit, which is what `git bisect run` does.
    10	
    11	To regenerate everything here, run `uv run python -m whodunit.simulate --out eval/simulator`. It takes about two minutes. `tables.md` has every number behind the charts, and `results.json` has the raw counts.
    12	
    13	## When good commits never fail
    14	
    15	![Accuracy against replay budget when good commits never fail](accuracy-clean-baseline.svg)
    16	
    17	Plain bisect with repeats wins here at every budget. For a bug that fails 30% of the time, 80 replays get it to 97% while the statistical bisect names the right commit in 67% of cases. The statistical bisect needs 160 replays to reach 93%.
    18	
    19	The reason is that plain bisect with repeats assumes a single failure convicts a commit, and in this world that is true. The statistical bisect does not assume it. It starts out believing a good commit fails about 5% of the time and spends replays finding out.
    20	
    21	Two things are worth knowing before picking plain bisect on that basis. Its mistakes are silent: with 40 replays on the 30% bug it names the wrong commit in 26% of cases and gives no sign of it, where the statistical bisect names the wrong one in 2% and says "not sure yet" in the rest. And the dashed line shows the statistical bisect's top suspect is right in 91% of cases at 80 replays, so most of its "not sure yet" answers are pointing at the culprit already.
    22	
    23	Plain bisect with one replay per commit is right 10% of the time on the 30% bug, at any budget.
    24	
    25	## When good commits fail 5% of the time on their own
    26	
    27	![Accuracy against replay budget when good commits fail 5% of the time](accuracy-flaky-baseline.svg)
    28	
    29	Agents are rarely this clean. Give every good commit a 5% chance of failing by itself and plain bisect with repeats falls apart, and more replays make it worse. On the 30% bug it is right in 31% of cases with 40 replays and 4% with 320, because every extra replay of an innocent commit is another chance for a stray failure to convict it. Even a bug that fails every time is found in only 46% of cases at 40 replays.
    30	
    31	The statistical bisect holds up. On the 30% bug it names the right commit in 60% of cases with 160 replays and 84% with 320. On a bug that fails every time it is right in 99% of cases and uses about 21 replays.
    32	
    33	## Where it falls short
    34	
    35	- A bug that fails 20% of the time on a flaky baseline is named in only 46% of cases, even with 320 replays. The top suspect is right in 70%.
    36	- The 95% bar is not always met. Across the cells, the share of cases with a wrong accusation runs from 0% to 7%, and the 7% is the 30% bug on a flaky baseline at 320 replays. The model assumes one change point and two fixed failure rates, and the prior on the good rate is a guess.
    37	- These are simulated commits with independent replays. Real replays share a model provider and a machine, so their failures can come in bursts, which this does not capture.
    38	- Small budgets are spent mostly on warming up. Below about 30 replays the statistical bisect rarely names anyone unless the bug fails every time.
    39	
    40	## What changed from the first design
    41	
    42	Two things, both found by simulating the 30% bug across 40 suspects with 300 replays allowed.
    43	
    44	The first version put a uniform prior on both failure rates, so it had to learn from scratch that good commits mostly pass. It solved 59% of cases. Starting from the belief that a good commit fails about 5% of the time, loosely held, took that to 93%.
    45	
    46	The brief said to test the commit that splits the posterior mass most evenly. The code now defaults to the replay with the highest expected information gain, and keeps the even split as `how="split"`. With the uniform prior the difference was large, 92% against 59%. With the current prior it is small: 282 cases solved against 280 out of 300, using 79 replays on average against 83. So the prior did the work, and the choice of picker barely matters.
---- eval/sealed/README.md
     1	# Sealed eval, 11 October 2026
     2	
     3	Five regressions were planted in the refund agent's history by a second coding session, through ordinary requests to fresh coding sessions. It wrote the answer key, and the key's SHA-256 was committed in 4c45f7f before Whodunit ran on any case. `eval/score.py` checks the key against that hash before scoring. The key was added to git only after every case had been run.
     4	
     5	Replays ran on the hackathon gateway's small model, three at a time.
     6	
     7	## Result
     8	
     9	With 120 replays allowed per case: 3 of 5 solved, 0 wrong accusations, 2 cases where nobody was named.
    10	
    11	The two open cases were then resumed from their own replays with up to 200 more allowed: 5 of 5 solved, 0 wrong accusations.
    12	
    13	| Case | Rate the second session measured | Rate Whodunit estimated | At 120 replays | In the end | Replays | Commits replayed | Suspects |
    14	| --- | ---: | ---: | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
    15	| cents-off | 100% | 93% | solved | solved | 21 | 5 | 13 |
    16	| wrong-order-refunded | 30% | 12% | nobody named | solved | 168 | 9 | 12 |
    17	| half-done-batch | 25% | 14% | nobody named | solved | 168 | 10 | 15 |
    18	| strangers-paid | 72% | 59% | solved | solved | 30 | 5 | 11 |
    19	| turned-away | 100% | 93% | solved | solved | 24 | 6 | 14 |
    20	
    21	The rate Whodunit estimates is a posterior mean, so after only a few replays it sits below 100% even for a bug that fails every time.
    22	
    23	## What it cost
    24	
    25	Replay spend on the gateway, estimated from token counts at list prices, came to about $1.91 for all five cases:
    26	
    27	- cents-off: about $0.08 (61,267 tokens)
    28	- wrong-order-refunded: about $0.57 (438,034 tokens)
    29	- half-done-batch: about $1.04 (795,110 tokens)
    30	- strangers-paid: about $0.10 (78,530 tokens)
    31	- turned-away: about $0.12 (100,111 tokens)
    32	
    33	## What this does and does not show
    34	
    35	- No commit was wrongly accused, at either budget. On `half-done-batch` the top suspect at 120 replays was the wrong commit, at 53%, and Whodunit named nobody. That is the behaviour the 95% bar is for.
    36	- The two cases it could not close at 120 replays are the two that fail least often. Whodunit put them at 12% and 14%, where the second session had measured 30% and 25% from a handful of probes. A bug that rare needs a lot of replays whatever the method.
    37	- The ranges are short, 11 to 15 suspects. On ranges this size a careful scan from the oldest commit would have replayed about as many commits as Whodunit did, so this eval says little about savings on long histories. The simulator in `eval/simulator` covers 40 suspects.
    38	- Five cases is a small sample. It is enough to say the pipeline works on a history it did not write, and not enough to put a number on accuracy.
    39	- Each case has one planted regression inside its range, by design. Two regressions that touch the same inputs in one range are outside what the model assumes.
    40	
    41	## What happened after the culprits were named
    42	
    43	The owner's ruling was patch for all three kinds of change involved. A fix counts as proven when its failure rate is back within 5 points of the rate before the culprit, at 95%.
    44	
    45	| Case | Outcome | Tries | Replays of the final fix |
    46	| --- | --- | ---: | --- |
    47	| cents-off | patched and proven | 1 | 0 failures in 30 |
    48	| strangers-paid | patched and proven | 1 | 0 failures in 30 |
    49	| wrong-order-refunded | patched and proven | 1 | 0 failures in 36 |
    50	| turned-away | two patches not proven, then reverted and proven | 3 | 0 failures in 30 |
    51	| half-done-batch | not fixed | 3 | two patches left 5 failures in 90 each, and the revert conflicts |
    52	
    53	So four of five were closed, one of them only by giving up on the patch the owner asked for, and one was left open and says so.
    54	
    55	## The same culprit across the whole history
    56	
    57	`cases/whole-history.toml` takes the `strangers-paid` regression and widens the range to the whole grown history, 57 suspects. With alibis from entire-graph for 22 of them and 18 ordinary runs as evidence, 20 replays across 5 commits named the culprit at 99.8%. A scan from the oldest suspect would have tested 37 commits. This is the run that speaks to savings on a longer history, and it is one run.
    58	
    59	## Against plain bisect with retries
    60	
    61	The same five cases were then given to plain bisect, with each commit replayed up to 5 times over and called bad on the first failure. It ran once per case, so this is one sample and not a rate.
    62	
    63	| Case | Plain bisect, 5 retries | Its replays | Statistical bisect | Its replays |
    64	| --- | --- | ---: | --- | ---: |
    65	| cents-off | right | 15 | right | 21 |
    66	| strangers-paid | right | 15 | right | 30 |
    67	| turned-away | right | 25 | right | 24 |
    68	| wrong-order-refunded | wrong commit named | 19 | right | 168 |
    69	| half-done-batch | could not start: the bad ref passed 10 replays in a row | 10 | right | 168 |
    70	
    71	On the three bugs that fail most of the time, plain bisect was right and used 55 replays in all against 75. That matches the simulator: with a clean baseline, and this one was clean (0 failures in 211 replays of commits before a culprit), plain bisect with retries is the cheaper tool.
    72	
    73	On the two bugs that fail about one run in eight, it went wrong in the two ways it can. For `wrong-order-refunded` a bad commit passed all 5 tries, the search went the wrong way, and it named an innocent commit three places from the real one, with nothing to say it was unsure. For `half-done-batch` the bad ref itself passed 10 replays in a row, so there was nothing to bisect.
    74	
    75	More retries would have fixed both, at a cost. The trouble is that the number has to be picked before the failure rate is known. The statistical bisect does not need it picked: it spent 21 to 30 replays on the frequent bugs and 168 on the rare ones, and on the rare ones it said "not sure yet" at 120 instead of naming someone.
